recentItems.title: Kyiv residents left reeling by end to pause in Russian attacks on capital
recentItems.description:
(9 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Kyiv, Ukraine - 8 September 2026
1. Various of burning building, smoke rising
2. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Sofiia Khodachynska, Kyiv resident:
++PARTLY COVERED BY SHOTS 3,4,5,6
"I arrived this morning and saw this horror. Now I don’t even know what to do next or whether we will continue working. The damage is clearly extensive. Everything burned down. This warehouse simply burned down, so I don’t know. I have mixed feelings. It’s very sad, very upsetting, because it was a job I loved. As they say, it’s gone. I don’t know. I can’t say anything because it’s a shock. I’m in shock."
3. Various of aftermath of strikes, destroyed buildings, cars, debris on street
4. Various of damaged buildings with black smoke rising
5. Various of people looking at burning building, smoke rising
6. Various of smoke rising from buildings
7. Yevhenii Yefremov outside a damaged residential building
8. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Yevhenii Yefremov, Kyiv resident:
++PARTLY COVERED BY SHOTS 9, 10, 11++
++AUDIO AS INCOMING++ 
“This is very sad. Before we were going to the shelter, but this time we did not have energy to go there. We try to leave Kyiv for the night, while we have the possibility." 
9. Smoke rising from ruined building
10. Various of damaged buildings
11. Various of crater on ground
12. Various of smoke rising
STORYLINE:
Two people were killed when Russia bombarded the Ukrainian capital Kyiv with drones and missiles overnight, local authorities said Tuesday, ending the pause on attacks between the warring countries as U.S. envoys made a renewed push towards a peace settlement over the weekend.

At least 16 people were wounded in Kyiv, Ukraine’s Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said. 

Explosions were heard in Kyiv for nearly five hours, according to Vyhivskyi. 

More than 50 sites were damaged in Kyiv during the Russian overnight attack, including residential buildings, dormitories, schools, shops, gas stations and a flour production plant, he said.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called it “a horrific attack” and accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of undermining U.S. peace efforts.

A Russian-installed official in illegally annexed Crimea said a Ukrainian attack killed two people there.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a post on Telegram that the attack was complex and appeared deliberately designed to cause maximum damage, involving ballistic and cruise missiles, anti-ship missiles and Shahed drones.

AP video by Vasilisa Stepanenko and Dan Bashakov

recentItems.title: Filmmaker Ilya Khrzhanovsky says Ukraine will win war; defends funding by Russian oligarch
recentItems.description:
(9 Sep 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
Venice - 9 September 2026
1. Wide of press conference
2. Medium pan (from left) editor Rob Myers, producer Swietlana Dragajewa-Turowska, producer Philippe Bober, cinematographer Jürgen Jürges, director Ilya Khrzhanovsky, actors Radmila Shchogolieva (with translator next to her), actor Maria Nafpliotou and writer/editor Ilya Permyakov
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Ilya Khrzhanovsky, writer/director:
"I think it's important to divide 'DAU' project, and 'DAU' movie. I start this movie 20 years ago and we finished the main shoot 2011, 15 years ago. And after that, I concentrate mostly on art project 'DAU,' which in this project include movies, installations, books and many other aspects. And I invite for my main cast another character, most important character - time - and I took time not to finish, not to touch the initial movie, which was already structured in a way how you can see it now is different, with different shooting blocks, with different stylistics, with more or less clear story. There's a lot of improvisation in dialogs. It's actually all the dialogs are improvised, but at the same time it was built structurally, like you can see it now. But the time change also my own perception on a way how I can talk about this and how I can edit it."
4. Wide of press conference
5. SOUNDBITE  (English) Ilya Khrzhanovsky, writer/director - on what he thinks of being criticized by the Ukraine’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Culture for the film's ties to Russian funding and the way Ukraine is portrayed in the film:
"I believe that Ukraine will survive, will stay strong and probably in that or other form will win on independency and beauty of the future. But at the moment, it's such a big attention that only what I can wish is a peace and success for Ukrainian government to succeed in the best possible way to save the country and to win this war. But I don't, I cannot give any comments about this in the kind of current political moment."
6. Wide of press conference
7. SOUNDBITE  (English) Ilya Khrzhanovsky, writer/director - on the film being financed by Russian oligarchs:
"Sergey Adonyev was not the first one who financed the movie. Not the last one. He financed 'DAU' project from 2008 till 2019. And his generous support was great and very important for the art part of the project. But, at that time, he was not under any kind of sanction list or anything. It was a completely different time. And last seven years, the project have completely different project, and the movie, have completely different life. And that's, as I told you, the movie was in a pause for most of the time when Mr. Adonyev financed the project. About Teodor Currentzis, yes I'm still in contact with him. I think he's one of the one of the greatest conductors of our time."
8. Wide of press conference
9. SOUNDBITE  (English) Ilya Khrzhanovsky, writer/director:
"My idea was that the genius is always a foreigner. And then I start to think who is a most interesting and talented foreigner who exist in the territory, Russian-speaking territory because I cast in Russia, I cast in Ukraine and cast in other countries. I cast Russian-speaking actors in Germany, for example. Here's my good friend and great actress Valery Tscheplanowa who is one of the best actresses in German theater and probably not so many people know that she is also speaking Russian. But I choose Teodor because his nature, because his energy, because his incredible talent. And also because he represents culture which exists longer than Abrahamic religion civilization."
10. Wide of press conference

STORYLINE:

recentItems.title: Cinema project bringing film screenings to Palestinian children in Gaza helps them 'escape hardship'
recentItems.description:
(9 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Gaza City, Gaza Strip — 8 September 2026
1. Various of children sitting near destruction, watching cartoons on screen ++NIGHT SHOT++
2. Various of girls sitting on the ground, with painted faces, watching cartoons on screen ++NIGHT SHOT++
3. Various of children sitting on rubble, watching
4. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Yafa Mashharawi, supervisor of children's cinema project: ++SOUNDBITE STARTS ON SHOT 4 AND IS OVERLAID BY SHOT 5 in PARTS++
“These film screenings travel throughout the Gaza Strip, from north to south, between tents and shelters. What we offer during these screenings is not only films but also recreational activities for children. We paint their faces to help them escape the atmosphere of destruction and war they have lived through and the emotions they have experienced, into a space of imagination and creativity.”
5. Various of displaced children sitting on the ground near destruction, some with painted faces, watching cartoons on screen
6. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Taghreed Jameel, displaced woman: ++SOUNDBITE STARTS ON SHOT 6 AND IS OVERLAID BY SHOT 7++
”The children are happy watching. I have grandchildren, and I brought them here so they could escape the hardship they've endured.”
7. Various of children sitting on rubble, watching
8. Various of displaced children watching cartoons ++NIGHT SHOT++
STORYLINE:
Children sat on the ground among massive piles of debris and rows of tents in Gaza City, their eyes fixed on a cartoon projected onto a screen. 

With their faces painted, some perched on higher mounds of rubble to get a better view.

The Little Wings Cinema Project, organized by Al-Mashharawi organization, has been bringing movie nights to displaced families across the Gaza Strip, with organizers holding a screening every two days in a different location to reach as many children as possible.

“These film screenings travel throughout the Gaza Strip, from north to south, between tents and shelters,” said Yafa Mashharawi, supervisor of the children's cinema project. 

Mashharawi added that there are also activities like face painting which serve as an "escape the atmosphere of destruction and war" for children.

For kids who have spent much of their lives amid war and displacement, the screenings offer a temporary break from their surroundings.

Taghreed Jameel, a displaced woman, brought her grandchildren to the show and said the "children are happy watching."

The vast majority of Gaza’s 2 million residents rely on aid groups for food, water, health care, shelter and other essentials after Israel’s two-year offensive destroyed much of the territory. 

Hundreds of thousands are living in tents, and reconstruction has yet to begin following a shaky ceasefire agreement reached in October.

Production by Wafaa Shurafa

recentItems.title: Eiffel Tower reopens after strike over limits on women staff during Hindu delegation visit
recentItems.description:
(9 Sep 2026) 
RESTRCTIONS SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
London - 9 September 2026
1. SOUNDBITE (English) Luke Garratt, The Associated Press:
"The Eiffel Tower has reopened, following a brief closure caused by a strike by workers who were protesting management instructions to limit women’s presence during a visit by a Hindu delegation. Management had told employees that female workers should “not be in contact” with a visiting delegation from the religious organisation B.A.P.S. The CGT union, which represents workers for the iconic tower, called the instructions “unnaceptable”, holding a one-day strike on Monday. 

ASSOCIATED PRESS   
Paris, France  - 8 September 2026
2. Various of Eiffel Tower
3. SOUNDBITE (French) Diane Davoine, CGT union personnel representative
“The employees, both men and women, are outraged. There's unanimity; a community has formed around this issue. There's no difference between employees. It's truly a collective outcry that has been expressed. 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
London - 9 September 2026
4. SOUNDBITE (English) Luke Garratt, The Associated Press:
"In a written statement to AP, BAPS said it had coordinated with the Eiffel Tower’s management to minimize disruption to staff and visitors ahead of the visit by the delegation of around 100 people. But it said the coordination was “never, at any point, intended as a request rooted in gender, and any suggestion to the contrary does not reflect the spirit or values of our fellowship or the delegation.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS   
Paris, France  - 8 September 2026
5. Various shots of the Eiffel Tower 
STORYLINE:
The Eiffel Tower reopened Tuesday, a day after one of the world’s most-visited landmarks was closed by a strike to protest what a union official called “unacceptable” management instructions limiting the presence of women during a visit by a Hindu delegation on Saturday.

Diane Davoine of the CGT union told The Associated Press anger grew among staff of the iconic 330-meter (1,083-foot) tower over the weekend after management told employees that female workers should ″not be in contact″ with a visiting delegation from Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha.

The group, known as BAPS, is a worldwide religious and civic organization within the Swaminarayan sect, a branch of Hinduism. It has been holding celebrations to mark the inauguration of a traditional Hindu stone temple in the French capital.

In a written statement emailed to the AP on Tuesday, the group said it coordinated with the Eiffel Tower’s management to minimize disruption to staff and visitors ahead of a visit by a delegation of some 100 people.

The coordination was “never, at any point, intended as a request rooted in gender, and any suggestion to the contrary does not reflect the spirit or values of our fellowship or the delegation,” the statement said.

BAPS said it “remains firmly committed to the principles of equality, mutual respect, and service to all, regardless of gender, background, or belief — values that lie at the very heart of our tradition’s teachings and community work worldwide.”

In an earlier statement, the group offered “sincere apologies to anyone who may have been hurt or inconvenienced by this situation.”

The company that operates the Eiffel Tower did not immediately comment. 

The 137-year-old tower is visited by some 7 million people each year.

Davoine said the tower often hosts special delegations, including U.S. President Donald Trump, visiting royals and celebrities like Britney Spears, and staff are happy to adapt.

recentItems.title: More schools close in Indonesia due to worsening haze from forest fires
recentItems.description:
(9 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Palembang, Indonesia - 9 Sept 2026
1. Wide of landmark of South Sumatra Province, Ampera bridge covered with haze
2. Wide of port of Palembang covered with haze
3. Wide of street of Palembang covered with haze as vehicles go by
4. Various exteriors of 222 elementary school of Palembang 
5. Wide of school teacher, Narwan Hamidi teaching through laptop with empty chairs stacked on top of desks
6. Mid of Hamidi teaching through laptop
7. Wide of empty class room
8. SOUNDBITE (Indonesian) Narwan Hamidi, elementary school teacher:
“Current weather conditions are very unfavorable for children, so it is better to conduct learning online, as the haze is detrimental to their health.”
9. Various of Putri Ramdhani learning at home through tablet
10. SOUNDBITE (Indonesian) Putri Ramdhani, elementary student:
“(We’re learning from home) due to the haze from forest and land fires.”
11. Wide of street of Palembang covered with haze
12. Various of haze on the streets of Palembang 
13. Wide of closed shops due to the haze
14. Mid of people commuting on the streets of Palembang 

STORYLINE:
Schools in the capital of Indonesia’s South Sumatra province switched to remote learning Wednesday as worsening haze from forest and peatland fires pushed air pollution to unhealthy levels, adding to disruptions that have already affected more than 1.4 million students across the country, officials said.

Indonesia has been plagued by forest and land fires for decades but an intensifying El Nino pattern and a prolonged dry season made the impact of the fires especially dire this year. 

Toxic haze and smoke have spread far beyond Indonesia’s borders in Southeast Asia, creating a regional health crisis. 

The smoke has drifted as far as the Philippines, more than 800 kilometers (500 miles) away, and breached Malaysia's emergency-level threshold, forcing authorities to declare an emergency last week in a town in Sarawak state on Borneo Island.

In Palembang, the capital city of South Sumatra province, schools from kindergarten to junior high were ordered to start conducting classes online Wednesday under an emergency measure.

Mayor Ratu Dewa said the thickening smoke posed health risks to children, including acute respiratory infections.

“Students’ health and safety remained the government’s priority,” Dewa said. 

Teachers were also asked to avoid excessive assignments during the period of remote learning, he said.

The policy, affecting more than 250,000 students at 1,030 schools in Palembang, will be reviewed regularly, and in-person classes will resume once conditions improve, he added.

Classrooms in the 222 elementary school of Palembang were empty as teachers like Narwan Hamidi started conducting classes virtually. 

"Current weather conditions are very unfavorable for children, so it is better to conduct learning online, as the haze is detrimental to their health," Hamidi said.

About 12,800 schools across Sumatra and Borneo islands remained closed as dangerous air quality persisted, according to government data.

Save the Children, a leading international non-government organization, said haze from wildfires, intensified by El Nino-driven dry conditions, has forced more than 1.4 million students into online learning in affected areas in Indonesia.


“The Earth, our home, is on fire, and children, including here in Asia, are being left to bear the consequences,” said Arshad Malik, Save the Children’s regional director for Asia.

recentItems.title: China MOFA Highlights - 9 September 2026
recentItems.description:
(9 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY: 

ASSOCIATED PRESS -  
Beijing, China -  09 September 2026

Spokesperson: Mao Ning

1.We have noted that there has recently been some hype surrounding the notion that China is pulling up the ladder, with some claiming that China is focused solely on its own development and has pulled away the ladder that other developing countries in the Global South rely on for their own progress. Do you have any comment on this “pulling up the ladder” theory? Improving oneself while benefiting others is a fundamental value underpinning China’s international cooperation. The so-called pulling up the ladder narrative finds no traction among countries of the Global South. China will always uphold the principles of mutual benefit, win-win outcomes, and shared development, serving as a trustworthy partner to countries of the Global South and contributing to the revitalization of the Global South through its own development.

2.Yesterday, the US cyber defense agency accused top Chinese AI lab incluidng Deepseek of stealing the capabilities of US models. It says that these campaigns form the core of China-based AI companies' strategies. Does the Foreign Ministry have any comments? I haven't read the specific report yet. But I can tell you that China’s development in artificial intelligence is the result of high-level scientific and technological self-reliance and self-strengthening. It has also benefited from our consistent adherence to the principles of collective consultation, joint contribution, and shared benefits, as well as open cooperation. We always believe that all countries should work together to strengthen cooperation to promote the open and inclusive development of AI for good and for all. We hope the US will earnestly implement the important consensus reached by the two leaders and not make unfounded accusations and smear against China. Both China and the US are major AI powers and should strengthen cooperation.

recentItems.title: Kyiv residents describe terror of overnight strike and grief of repeated loss from Russian attacks
recentItems.description:
(9 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY: 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Kyiv, Ukraine - 09 September 2026
1. Destroyed residential building
2. Emergency worker cleaning debris 
3. Rescuers pointing at some houses
4. Emergency worker throwing damaged parts 
5. Parts of the facade falling down
6. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Katerina Slobodianiuk, Kyiv resident:
“Oh, we’re actually from the building at 23 Orlivska Street, where a missile struck. A month before that, a Shahed drone flew near our building, hit a construction crane, and crashed. Three of our cars were damaged. After that, we moved here, and now a Shahed has struck here, too.”
7. Various of local residents
8. SOUNDBTE (Ukrainian) Olha Smal, Kyiv resident:
“Suddenly, I was thrown across the kitchen by this powerful wave. And I realized that something had hit the apartment. It’s a three-room apartment. There were flames immediately, and the smell of smoke. I ran to the third room, and everything was already on fire. I started calling for help and looking for my cat. He had disappeared somewhere. Then I went to the neighbor across the hall. She is pregnant, and she was also injured, debris hit her, and there was broken glass.”
9. Damaged residential building
10. SOUNDBTE (Ukrainian) Olha Smal, Kyiv resident: 
“Within just a few minutes, the smell of smoke was so strong that I couldn’t think straight anymore. Unfortunately, the emergency services couldn’t save my cat. I took him to a clinic, but unfortunately, they couldn’t save him. He was like a psychologist for me. My son died a year and three months ago. The cat was always waiting for me until I came home. It’s very hard. The orcs (slang term referring to Russians as the monsters from "The Lord of the Rings") will pay for everything.”
11. Emergency serviceman dismantling debris 
12. SOUNDBTE(Ukrainian) Olha Smal, 62, Kyiv resident:
"How much more can you endure? In 2023, my father died. In 2024, my mother. In 2025, my son was killed. I don’t know how much more grief there will be. This war. How are you supposed to endure all of this? I want peace. I want everyone to be alive and healthy. I live for my granddaughters, for my older son. I want to believe that everything will be all right in Ukraine. Now you live one day at a time. You don’t know what will happen to you tomorrow, or even what will happen today. It’s very, very hard."
13. Rescuers removing damaged car
14. Various of local residents
15. Damaged residential building and children's playground
STORYLINE:
Four people were injured when a Russian attack damaged a 22-story residential building in Kyiv’s Darnytskyi district, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Wednesday.

The attack damaged the 11th and 12th floors and sparked a fire on the 12th floor.

Kyiv resident Kateryna Slobodianiuk said the building was her family’s new home after their previous residence was damaged in a Russian attack. She said a Shahed drone had struck near their former building a month earlier, damaging three of their cars.

“We’re actually from the building at 23 Orlivska St., where a missile struck,” Slobodianiuk told The Associated Press. “After that, we moved here, and now a Shahed has struck here too.”

62-year-old Olha Smal said the attack injured her neighbors and killed her cat. She also described losing her father in 2023, her mother in 2024 and her son in 2025.

recentItems.title: Suspected measles cases kill nearly 1,000 as Bangladesh struggles to contain outbreak
recentItems.description:
(9 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Dhaka, Bangladesh - 6 September 2026
1. Wide and pan of measles ward at Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute
2. Mid of Ranu Akhter showing toy to her daughter Rojatun Jannat Ramisa while she receives oxygen through mask
3. Various of children receiving oxygen through masks
4. SOUNDBITE (Bangla) Ranu Akhter, mother of measles patient Rojatun Jannat Ramisa:
"Fourteen days ago, when we were at the district hospital, there were other children being treated alongside my daughter. I saw that those children also had red rashes on their bodies, sores in their mouths and fever. Seeing these things, I realized (It was measles)."
5. Various of doctors and nurses providing treatment in measles ward
6. Mid of IV bag hanging from IV pole beside patient's bed
7. SOUNDBITE (Bangla) Professor Dr. Md. Atiqul Islam, neonate and child specialist, Bangladesh Shishu Hospital & Institute:
"For the past six months, we have been treating measles patients continuously, and we are exhausted. The measles outbreak has now declined significantly, but we are not completely free of it yet. The measles patients who are now coming to our children’s hospital are arriving with serious complications, especially pneumonia, diarrhea and encephalitis. Most of the patients are suffering from pneumonia."
8. Wide of exterior of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute
9. Mid of guardians gathered in front of doctor's chamber with patients to secure consultation
10. SOUNDBITE (Bangla) Professor Dr. Md. Atiqul Islam, neonate and child specialist, Bangladesh Shishu Hospital & Institute:
"During the COVID period in 2021 and 2022, we did not go out of our homes, and many of us did not take our children to get vaccinated. So, if you look at children who are now four or five years old, many of them missed their vaccinations. That created a gap. During the previous interim government, vaccines were also unavailable at many vaccination centers. Guardians went once or twice but could not get the vaccines. They may have been told to come back later, but many of them did not return. Because of these gaps, our routine measles vaccination coverage, which we used to say was around 95%, or at least above 90%, fell to below 50%. That is why we have had this outbreak."
11. Various of guardians holding children in their laps inside measles ward
12. SOUNDBITE (Bangla) Professor Dr. Md. Atiqul Islam, neonate and child specialist, Bangladesh Shishu Hospital & Institute:
"This year, the government has started giving the measles vaccine from six months of age, instead of the previous schedule starting at nine months. Even children who have already received a measles vaccine are being advised to receive an additional dose if at least one month has passed since their previous dose. This applies to children from six months to five years of age."
13. Various of nurse administering treatment to Saif Hasan, 1 month and 20 days old, while his father Saiful Islam and mother Laizu Akhter assist
14. Various of guardians with their children
15. SOUNDBITE (Bangla) Saiful Islam, father of measles patient Saif Hasan:
"Sores developed in the child’s mouth, and the body became almost completely red. But at that time, they did not tell us anything about whether the child might have measles. After treating the child for several days, they referred us to Dhaka. When we brought the child to this hospital in Dhaka, the doctor examined the child and told us that it was measles."
16. Mid of IV bag and children's clothes hanging from IV pole beside patient's bed
